trace_issues.name: SQLCODE
trace_issues.message: SQLCODE (tested at lines 76, 94, 119, 138 and moved at 92, 123, 143) has no registered Field ID: the system's SQLCA.cpy (SYS-PORTFOLIO-001-FIL-0017) defines only SQL-STATUS-CODES. SQLCODE is the DB2-supplied SQLCA field; target_id kept null
WS-CONNECTION-STATE has no VALUE clause and is set only inside 1000-CONNECT and 3000-CHECK-STATUS; a DISC request relies on the state left in WORKING-STORAGE by a previous call of this subprogram

program_narrative: DB2CONN is a called subprogram (DB2 connection manager) that performs one DB2 connection service per call, selected by the 4-character function code in the caller's LS-DB2-REQUEST area. For 'CONN' it copies the database and plan names from the request and issues SQL CONNECT, retrying up to WS-MAX-RETRIES times (initial value 3) and calling the external routine DELAY with DB2-RETRY-WAIT between failed attempts. For 'DISC' it commits outstanding work and issues CONNECT RESET, but only when its saved connection state says it is connected. For 'STAT' it probes the connection with SELECT CURRENT SERVER and records whether the connection is active. It returns results to the caller in LS-RETURN-CODE (0 success, 4 connection not active, 8 disconnect error, 12 connect failure or invalid function) together with LS-SQLCODE and an LS-ERROR-MSG text. An unrecognised function code is reported to the common error processor ERRPROC. The program reads no files and writes none; all database access is through embedded SQL.

paragraphs.name: 0000-MAIN
pseudocode: -- Entry point: dispatch the caller's request by function code (LS-FUNCTION)
SELECT CASE requested_function  -- EVALUATE TRUE over the 88-levels of LS-FUNCTION
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
-- Entry point: dispatch the caller's request by function code (LS-FUNCTION)
SELECT CASE requested_function  -- EVALUATE TRUE over the 88-levels of LS-FUNCTION
  WHEN 'CONN' (FUNC-CONN):
    CALL 1000-connect
  WHEN 'DISC' (FUNC-DISC):
    CALL 2000-disconnect
  WHEN 'STAT' (FUNC-STAT):
    CALL 3000-check-status
  ELSE:
    SET error_text = 'Invalid function code'
    CALL 9000-error-routine
END SELECT
RETURN to caller  -- GOBACK

annotations.note: ERR-TEXT belongs to the ERR-MESSAGE record of copybook ERRHAND, which 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE passes to ERRPROC

paragraphs.name: 1000-CONNECT
pseudocode: -- Connect to DB2, retrying up to max_retries times
SET connection_state = DISCONNECTED  -- SET WS-DISCONNECTED TO TRUE ('N')
SET ws_db_name = ls_db_name  -- database name supplied by the caller
SET ws_plan_name = ls_plan_name  -- plan name supplied by the caller
WHILE NOT (connection_state = CONNECTED OR retry_count >= max_retries) DO  -- inline PERFORM UNTIL, condition tested before each pass
SQL CONNECT TO database named in ws_db_name
IF retry_count < max_retries AND connection_state is not CONNECTED THEN
PASSING: db2_retry_wait  -- external wait routine, not in the inventory; wait value from DBPROC copybook
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
-- Connect to DB2, retrying up to max_retries times
SET connection_state = DISCONNECTED  -- SET WS-DISCONNECTED TO TRUE ('N')
CLEAR retry_count  -- initialise to zero
SET ws_db_name = ls_db_name  -- database name supplied by the caller
SET ws_plan_name = ls_plan_name  -- plan name supplied by the caller
WHILE NOT (connection_state = CONNECTED OR retry_count >= max_retries) DO  -- inline PERFORM UNTIL, condition tested before each pass
  SQL CONNECT TO database named in ws_db_name
  IF sqlcode = 0 THEN  -- CHECK SQLCODE
    SET connection_state = CONNECTED  -- 'Y'
    SET ls_return_code = 0
  ELSE
    INCREMENT retry_count BY 1
    CALL 1100-handle-conn-error
  END IF
  IF retry_count < max_retries AND connection_state is not CONNECTED THEN
    CALL program DELAY
      PASSING: db2_retry_wait  -- external wait routine, not in the inventory; wait value from DBPROC copybook
  END IF
END WHILE

annotations.note: Inline PERFORM ... END-PERFORM (lines 69-88): the loop body is in this paragraph; no other paragraph is executed except 1100-HANDLE-CONN-ERROR on failure
WS-PLAN-NAME is copied from the request but not used by any SQL statement in this program
DELAY is not in the file registry; wait behaviour cannot be traced statically

paragraphs.name: 1100-HANDLE-CONN-ERROR
pseudocode: -- Record a failed connection attempt for the caller
SET ls_error_msg = 'Network error connecting to DB2'
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
-- Record a failed connection attempt for the caller
SET ls_sqlcode = sqlcode
SELECT CASE sqlcode
  WHEN -30081:
    SET ls_error_msg = 'Maximum connections exceeded'
  WHEN -99999:
    SET ls_error_msg = 'Network error connecting to DB2'
  ELSE:
    SET ls_error_msg = 'General DB2 connection error'
END SELECT
SET ls_return_code = 12  -- connection failure

annotations.note: Runs once per failed attempt; the last failure's SQLCODE and message are what the caller sees

paragraphs.name: 2000-DISCONNECT
pseudocode: -- Commit work and release the DB2 connection, only if this program holds one
SQL COMMIT WORK  -- make pending database changes permanent
SQL CONNECT RESET  -- disconnect from the current DB2 server
IF sqlcode = 0 THEN  -- CHECK SQLCODE of CONNECT RESET; the COMMIT result is not tested
END IF  -- when not connected nothing is done and ls_return_code is left as received
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
-- Commit work and release the DB2 connection, only if this program holds one
IF connection_state = CONNECTED THEN
  SQL COMMIT WORK  -- make pending database changes permanent
  SQL CONNECT RESET  -- disconnect from the current DB2 server
  IF sqlcode = 0 THEN  -- CHECK SQLCODE of CONNECT RESET; the COMMIT result is not tested
    SET connection_state = DISCONNECTED
    SET ls_return_code = 0
  ELSE
    SET ls_sqlcode = sqlcode
    SET ls_error_msg = 'Error disconnecting from DB2'
    SET ls_return_code = 8
  END IF
END IF  -- when not connected nothing is done and ls_return_code is left as received

annotations.note: SQLCODE is not checked after COMMIT WORK; only the CONNECT RESET result decides the return code

paragraphs.name: 3000-CHECK-STATUS
pseudocode: -- Check whether the DB2 connection is active by asking the server for its name
SQL SELECT CURRENT SERVER FROM SYSIBM.SYSDUMMY1 INTO ws_db_name
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
-- Check whether the DB2 connection is active by asking the server for its name
SQL SELECT CURRENT SERVER FROM SYSIBM.SYSDUMMY1 INTO ws_db_name
IF sqlcode = 0 THEN  -- CHECK SQLCODE
  SET connection_state = CONNECTED
  SET ls_return_code = 0
ELSE
  SET connection_state = DISCONNECTED
  SET ls_sqlcode = sqlcode
  SET ls_error_msg = 'DB2 connection not active'
  SET ls_return_code = 4
END IF

annotations.note: The status probe overwrites WS-DB-NAME with the current server name

paragraphs.name: 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE
pseudocode: -- Report an invalid request to the common error processor
PASSING: err_message  -- ERR-MESSAGE record from copybook ERRHAND
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
-- Report an invalid request to the common error processor
SET err_program = 'DB2CONN'
SET ls_return_code = 12
CALL program ERRPROC
  PASSING: err_message  -- ERR-MESSAGE record from copybook ERRHAND
